example_summary: Taxability of ₹ 5 lacs rent received by Ankur from Yahoo Movies Ltd. for film shooting on agricultural land.
source_provision:
### Statutory Matrix: Agricultural Income vs. Non-Agricultural Use

| Statutory Provision / Precedent | Legal Benchmark / Operational Test | Tax Treatment & Classification |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 10(1)** | Exempts **Agricultural Income** from total income. | **Exempt Income** |
| **Section 2(1A)(a) & (b)** | Requires rent/revenue to be derived directly from land used for **agricultural purposes**. | Must satisfy **nexus test** |
| ***CIT v. Raja Benoy Kumar Sahas Roy*** | Income requires performance of **basic agricultural operations** (tilling, sowing, planting). | Statutory Benchmark |
| ***B. Nagi Reddi v. CIT*** | Revenue from permitting film shooting on land lacks nexus with agricultural operations. | **Taxable Income** |


### Statutory Checklist for Section 2(1A) Compliance

* **Direct Nexus Rule:** The income must be directly derived from land situated in India used for agricultural purposes.
* **Operational Test:** The income must arise directly from basic agricultural operations or sale of agricultural produce.


> [!WARNING] Judicial Precedent Benchmark
> Land merely being characteristically agricultural is insufficient. If the primary source of revenue is a non-agricultural contract (e.g., film shooting charges), it is classified as **Income from Other Sources** under **Section 56**.
